document_title: Abraham Lincoln to Truman Smith, Saturday, November 10, 1860 (Lincoln will not issue a public statement to reassure the South)
author: Abraham Lincoln
claims: A circular distributed before the election by respectable citizens of New York held up Lincoln as a dangerous radical and an enemy of the institutions of the South and of the peace and security of the Union, whose policies were unsettling to the commercial life of the country.
Such a message was typical of the sort of vituperation a presidential candidate must endure.
Such a message was especially unsettling in the current campaign.
Such a message would have a negative influence in the South as well as among Northern voters.
